assessment: The binding axis is interaction-breadth: one permanent class answered of five, with artifact, enchantment, graveyard and land all uncovered. Two picks close it outright — adding Assassin's Trophy and Dawnhand Dissident and recomputing the axis gives five of five, the cited target exactly. The rest of the ten goes to the engine's thinnest component, the free repeatable -1/-1 source that stands at three cards, and to the two single-card points of failure downstream of it. No slot here buys mana or generic draw: ramp is the only axis over target and is where half the cuts come from.

ten.why: Recomputing interaction-breadth with this one card added takes the deck from one answered class to four — creature, artifact, enchantment, land — which is the difference between beating and losing to a turn-3 Cursed Totem, an artifact that switches off Yawgmoth, Carrion Feeder, Viscera Seer, Devoted Druid and every mana dork in one card; the corpus is blunt about the order to buy in: "Breadth before depth: three opponents mean every permanent type appears, so cover the classes — creature, artifact, enchantment, graveyard, land — before doubling any; catch-all removal earns its premium".
ten.unlocks: The deck's first answer to a noncreature permanent, at instant speed and two mana — inside the three-mana ceiling the same section reports as "essentially the most any player should pay for interaction".

ten.closes: interaction-breadth, and the engine's ignition component (free repeatable -1/-1 source, 3 cards)
ten.why: One black mana buys both halves of what this deck is short of: "{T}, Blight 1: Surveil 1" is a free repeatable -1/-1 placement — put the counter on a Snake, Hapatra mints the replacement, Blood Artist drains, the board is flat and you filtered a card — and the second mode, "{T}, Blight 2: Exile target card from a graveyard", is the fifth permanent class, so the recomputed breadth with this beside Assassin's Trophy is five of five.
ten.unlocks: Targeted graveyard hate that does not tax your own Eternal Witness, Phyrexian Reclamation or Svogthos the way a Rest in Peace effect would; one activation a turn, so the surveil and the exile compete for the same tap.

ten.closes: the engine's ignition component (free repeatable -1/-1 source, 3 cards)
ten.why: A 0/4 for {2}{B} that draws a card and blights 1 at every one of your end steps: from turn 4 on that is a free Snake and a free card every turn cycle, an Insect too under Nest of Scarabs and a drain under Obelisk Spider, and its own body soaks three of the counters before it dies into an outlet.
ten.unlocks: A counter source that costs no mana on the turn you use it — but on a fixed trigger, so unlike Yawgmoth's activation you cannot hold it up in response to a removal spell; "Payoffs without the enabler are blanks until the engine exists", and this is an enabler.

ten.closes: the engine's ignition component (free repeatable -1/-1 source, 3 cards)
ten.why: Landfall proliferate is a free counter multiplier on a deck that makes its turn-3 land drop 90.2% of the time — every -1/-1 counter already on the board gets a twin and every twin is a Hapatra trigger — and because proliferate is chosen permanent by permanent you skip Devoted Druid and take Scurry Oak's +1/+1 while you are there.
ten.unlocks: Repeatable arrowhead counters back onto Serrated Arrows for zero mana, which is the one job Contagion Clasp does that nothing else in the 99 repeats, and it does it without paying {4} and a tap.

ten.closes: single point of failure: Mikaeus, the Unhallowed (1 card)
ten.why: No creature in the 99 returns itself, so Yawgmoth eats whatever the board happens to be holding; a one-mana Zombie you recast from the graveyard every turn — legal here because Carrion Feeder, Host of the Hereafter and Mikaeus are each Zombies — is fodder on tap from turn 2 and never asks Mikaeus for undying.
ten.unlocks: A sacrifice loop that survives Mikaeus being answered, and two three-card lines whose other pieces are already sleeved.

ten.closes: interaction-breadth — in Magic terms only; see the caveat in `why`
ten.why: Channel destroys an artifact, an enchantment or a nonbasic land at instant speed for {1}{G}, and {G} with Hapatra alone on the battlefield since the ability costs {1} less per legendary creature — that is an answer you can still cast under the tax, which the corpus names the hard case: "Stax is the hardest breadth test: a counter answers a lock piece only on the way in, so some answers must be castable under the tax"; read the number honestly, though, because the breadth axis only reads cards carrying an interactive role and this one is filed land:utility, so adding it leaves the measured breadth at one.
ten.unlocks: Three answered classes out of a land slot rather than a spell slot, at zero cost to the 36-land count and none to the zero-tapland count.

ten.closes: engine component: any drain converter (4 cards, 51.9% assembled)
ten.why: Of the four drain converters in the 99 only Zulaport Cutthroat and Bastion of Remembrance hit every seat — Blood Artist picks one player and Blasting Station pings one target — and this triggers on any creature dying anywhere, so a Toxic Deluge or an opponent's own wrath becomes table-wide life loss; "each-opponent drains are the payoffs that actually scale".
ten.unlocks: A third table-wide converter that is also a deathtouch reach blocker, fetchable by Worldly Tutor, Green Sun's Zenith and Survival of the Fittest — the eight-card tutor class turns a creature into a toolbox slot in a way it cannot turn an enchantment.

ten.closes: single point of failure: Mikaeus, the Unhallowed (1 card)
ten.why: A sacrificed Snake token ceases to exist and comes back as nothing, so on an empty board Yawgmoth is a blank; {1}{B} at instant speed returns this one from the graveyard for the rest of the game, and both of its listed lines run off Pitiless Plunderer plus an altar already in the 99.
ten.unlocks: Fodder that survives the token rule, so the free outlets have something to eat in the turns after a wrath.

ten.closes: the engine's ignition component (free repeatable -1/-1 source, 3 cards)
ten.why: Three opponents means three upkeeps, so this is up to three free -1/-1 placements and three points of life loss per turn cycle without ever asking you for mana — three Snakes, three Insects under Nest of Scarabs, three drains under Obelisk Spider — and when it finally dies persist returns it carrying a -1/-1 counter, which is one more Hapatra trigger on the way back.
ten.unlocks: Counters placed on the opponents' side of the board, which no other source in the deck does at will; it is gated on each opponent controlling a creature, so it is worth most against a board and least against the combo deck racing you.

ten.closes: engine component: any drain converter (4 cards, 51.9% assembled)
ten.why: Both sweepers in the 99 erase your own board and hand you nothing back; this one stays on the battlefield afterwards and drains every opponent for each creature you lose, so X=1 with six Snakes out is an eighteen-point swing across the table and the converter is still there for the rebuild.
ten.unlocks: A drain converter no creature wrath can answer — and a caution: it modifies power and toughness rather than placing counters, so unlike Black Sun's Zenith it mints no Snakes and feeds neither Nest of Scarabs nor Necroskitter.

gaps: Blowfly Infestation is a one-card point of failure with no closer, and a whole-pool scan agrees with the engine's own reading: of the 31 B/G Commander-legal cards whose oracle text carries both 'dies' and '-1/-1 counter', none repeatably chains a placement off another creature's death — Festering Mummy and Boggart Mischief fire once. The nearest same-shape effect is already sleeved: Host of the Hereafter moves counters on a death. Hapatra + Blowfly has never had a stack scenario; /resolve-stack is the route.

Nothing in this colour identity reproduces Yawgmoth's property — free, at-will, unbounded, any target. The whole-pool scan of activated -1/-1 placements returns Fevered Convulsions (at-will and unbounded, but {2}{B}{B} an activation), Grim Poppet and Liliana, Death Wielder at seven mana, and three bounded artifacts. Every ignition pick above meets the weaker property, free once a turn, and says so in its entry.

Boseiju, Who Endures and Bojuka Bog answer classes this deck cannot answer, out of land slots, and the breadth axis cannot see either: it reads only cards carrying an interactive role, and those two are land:utility and land:tapped. Recomputed, adding Boseiju leaves breadth at one of five. The cards work; the number does not move, and a prescription sized on that number would be sized on nothing.

Gravecrawler + Phyrexian Altar is listed as a two-card line and is not one: recasting from the graveyard needs a second Zombie on the battlefield. Carrion Feeder, Host of the Hereafter and Mikaeus each satisfy it, so the line is live here — but the three-card Pitiless Plunderer records name their enabler outright and are the safer citation. Neither has had a stack scenario.

Nim Deathmantle sits on the engine's own closer list for the Mikaeus component and is left off deliberately: +2/+2 lifts this deck's 1/1 tokens out of range of a single -1/-1 counter, the same anti-synergy that is open against Mikaeus's own anthem. Nothing has settled it, and a stack scenario should.

Card-advantage reads 8 against a floor of 10, and the audit's probe names Grim Backwoods, The One Ring and Yawgmoth as showing the function uncounted. That is a question, not a hole, so no slot here buys generic draw.

Mox Amber is listed in the obsolescence index as a strictly-better Lotus Petal and still does not make the ten: ramp is the deck's only OVER axis, so an upgrade inside it closes nothing the diagnosis named. Beast Within is off for a related reason — it duplicates the coverage Assassin's Trophy already buys, for one more mana, and hands an opponent a 3/3 that costs three Yawgmoth activations to undo.

The cuts are ten separate proposals, not a set. Five of them come from the ramp axis, which reads 16 against a 10-12 band — but five of those 16 copies (Ashnod's Altar, Phyrexian Altar, Pitiless Plunderer, Deadly Dispute, Devoted Druid) are engine pieces the taxonomy files as ramp, and three of the five cuts are mana dorks, which are part of why Hapatra lands on turn 2 in 9,970 of 10,000 goldfish runs. Take one or two; sweeping them would price a swap against a number the deck does not really have.

No deck_recon.json exists for this deck, so nothing here is grounded in what other Hapatra lists actually run. Inclusion rates would settle whether a five-class interaction suite is the norm for this commander or whether this list is the outlier.
